plan.rationale: Objective is latency_ms for one complete single-GPU batch=32 offline inference bounded by torch.cuda.synchronize() after the forward. The torch collector already ran and resolved GPU-side attribution completely (coverage.json: 88/88 CUDA kernels associated, 0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous forward sequences, 0 backward/autograd ranges), so torch is not re-requested and nsys is not selected: no open overlap, graph-tracing or attribution question remains on this single timeline with no CUDA graphs. The one unmeasured latency dimension is the host-side share of the measured window, so python_runtime is selected to decompose host dispatch and binding costs (per-layer Python and transformers wrapper frames) that the kernel-associated trace cannot split; it runs in a separate warmed cProfile pass, and its inclusive/self times will be used only as diagnostic host-cost evidence, never as performance scores or GPU compute durations. All communication-oriented collectors are excluded on observed evidence: capability field communication=not_applicable (single-device task), no process group or NCCL in the workload, so nccl_tuning and collective_calibration have no collectives to observe, and execution_timeline's multi-device CPU-to-CUDA submit, per-device interval and gradient callback machinery is redundant with the already-complete association and has no buckets to correlate. device_telemetry is excluded because its device-wide NVML utilization/memory samples have native windows that cannot attribute per-call latency, duplicate the peak_allocated_bytes the harness already records per sample, and no PCIe transfer occurs inside the measured region.
